version.changelog: Initial release: TIPS/소상공인/R&D 정부지원사업 JSONL 수집기

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requested resources are consistent with a web-scraper for Korean government program pages; it does not request credentials or contact unexpected endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (collect Korean government support programs) match the included scripts. The code only fetches public government sites and writes JSONL outputs; no unrelated services, binaries, or credentials are required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the included Python and shell scripts against an output directory. The runtime instructions and scripts only read/write local output/checkpoint files and fetch HTML from listed government domains. There is no instruction to read unrelated system files, credentials, or to transmit data to third-party endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with included scripts (no install spec). No remote downloads, package installs, or archive extraction are present—risk from install mechanism is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials and the code does not attempt to read secrets. Network access to public websites is necessary and proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not alter other skills, and only writes its own output and .checkpoint.json into the user-specified output directory. Autonomous invocation is platform-default and not specifically elevated here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward scraper for public Korean government pages and is internally consistent. Before running: (1) review and run the scripts in a controlled environment (e.g., container) so output goes to a non-sensitive directory, (2) run with a small --max-pages to validate behavior, (3) be aware several sources are skipped because they require JS rendering—if you add a headless browser, keep its use limited and avoid supplying credentials, and (4) ensure your use complies with target sites' robots.txt and terms and respect rate limits (script sleeps 0.8s between requests).
